subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should runtime-enforced operator visibility be a core default across channels, an opt-in per-channel/provider capability, or split into narrower delivery-confirmation and watchdog contracts first?
rationale: The requested behavior changes channel-visible defaults, introduces new config/default surfaces, and can affect duplicate delivery, quiet/final-only semantics, and operator alerting; automation cannot choose that product policy safely.

options.title: Split And Decide Contracts
options.body: Use the maintainer-owned durable final fallback contract plus a focused watchdog contract to define defaults, config, conformance tests, and rollout before implementation.

options.title: Approve Core Default
options.body: Make a gateway-owned watchdog and response-delivery confirmation default across durable channels, accepting the extra messages and migration/proof burden as a safety feature.

options.title: Make It Opt-In
options.body: Add per-channel or per-agent operator-visibility settings so existing final-only/quiet behavior remains unchanged until users enable watchdog and delivery alerts.

recommendation.title: Split And Decide Contracts
recommendation.body: Use the maintainer-owned durable final fallback contract plus a focused watchdog contract to define defaults, config, conformance tests, and rollout before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the strongest related maintainer-authored delivery contract and are best positioned to decide how that contract should combine with watchdog behavior.
